title: All-to-all, 4-group Boardfly (128 chips)
intro:
All-to-all sends a different piece of data from every chip to every other chip, and nothing is added up. Mixture-of-experts models use it to send each token to the chip holding its expert, and back. Every piece travels its own path, so the cost is set by how many hops paths take and how evenly they spread over the links. Each dot is one piece; click a chip to follow only its traffic.

Boardfly keeps paths short as the slice grows: at most 7 hops at 1,024 chips (6.5 on average), against 16 at most (8 on average) on an 8x8x16 torus. At these small sizes the two are close: 3.0 hops on average on the 64-chip torus, 3.2 on this 128-chip slice.

G.name: fiber through the OCS, between groups

segments: Every chip sends to all 127 others at once over minimal paths. Paths average 3.2 hops, at most 5, and cross at most one fiber link.
